Subject: Pharmex: configurable retention + region controls — runbook & erasure authority

Hi Aisha / Pharmex team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Pharmex needs: (1) per-tenant configurable retention presets (30/90/365/indefinite) exposed in the Console/API, and (2) the ability to bind storage + KMS keys to a region for regulatory sovereignity. Two urgent asks from Procurement & Security: a one-page runbook for how we will handle customer erasure requests and a statement of who has authority to approve cross-region erasures (i.e., when customer data must be deleted in all replicas).

Attached is a draft data residency matrix where Pharmex mapped desired settings to sample tenant types — please use it as the source of truth for scope. Can the product + eng team confirm feasibility and whether we need a short spike to validate behavior for KV cache + cross-region fallback?

Immediate asks: 
- Karthik / Markus: high level feasibility (API surface, timeline, constraints) by EOD Wed PT.
- Monica: runbook owner — please draft initial erasure flow (we discussed including the audit steps and DocuSign authorization) and share with Aisha by Thu.
- Aisha / Procurement: confirm whether Pharmex requires key residency (customer-managed KMS) or if redwood-managed regional keys are acceptable.

Attachments: pharmex-data-residency-matrix.xlsx, erasure-runbook-draft.md

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Pharmex: configurable retention + region controls — runbook & erasure authority

Camila / Aisha —

Quick technical read on the asks: overall feasible but a few non-obvious tradeoffs that will affect rollout timing. Key points: 

1) Retention presets: we can expose per-tenant presets via the Admin API and Console. This requires adding a retention policy object with a default fallthrough behavior; need decision: when a tenant-level preset exists, should workspace-level or route-level overrides be allowed? If yes, complexity increases (~+2 weeks).

2) Regional storage + KMS: we support region tagging today but not per-tenant KMS selection. Implementing customer-managed KMS per-tenant will touch infra (key wrapping, cross-region replication locks). If Pharmex insists on customer-managed KMS for EU/US segmentation, estimate 4-6 week effort with infra coordination. Redwood-managed regional keys (with attestations) reduces effort to ~2 weeks.

3) Erasure flow: we can automate a purge job but must be careful with KV cache and asynchronous replication. Proposed sequence: mark records for erase -> quiesce write paths -> perform cryptographic deletion (revoke keys) + logical purge -> confirm via audit log and notify customer. Need to confirm deletion SLAs (e.g., 72 hours vs 30 days).

I created a spike ticket JIRA-INF-3245 to validate replication/kv-cache behavior on a small model (llama-v2-13b). If stakeholders want the spike run before a roadmap commitment, we'll need 3 business days.

Questions for Pharmex: default fallthrough behavior, deletion SLA, and KMS preference.

Karthik / Team —

Agree with Karthik's assessment. A few implementation constraints and a proposed timeline: 

- MVP scope: Console + Admin API to set per-tenant retention presets + region tag on storage buckets. No workspace-level overrides to keep surface area small for MVP.
- KMS: recommend Redwood-managed regional keys for initial delivery. If Pharmex needs CMK (customer-managed keys), treat it as an enterprise add-on with separate rollout.
- Erasure authority: define two roles: Customer-initiated erasure (customer can request via Console or signed DocuSign) and Redwood-initiated forced erasure (only on compliance/legal escalation, requires SOC/Legal approval). We will need an internal approval workflow (CS -> Security -> Legal) recorded in the audit trail.

Estimated timeline (MVP):
- Spike (replication + KV cache) — 3 business days (INF-3245)
- Engineering implementation — 4 weeks sprint-equivalents (API + backend + Console)
- QA + compliance signoff — 1 week

I'll attach a short impact note for infra dependencies. If Pharmex wants KMS CMK, add +4 weeks and a security-led review.
